title: smoke_TestGather test_gather crashes with Windows access violation (signal 3221225477) on CPU FP16 GatherV2 batch_dims=-2
signature: OpenVINO process crashed with signal 3221225477 (access violation) during test_tf_Gather.py::TestGather::test_gather CPU FP16 GatherV2 batch_dims=-2 axis=-1|Code Issue

failed_jobs.name: TensorFlow Layer Tests / TensorFlow Layer Tests
failed_jobs.symptom: pytest subprocess running inference was killed with Windows exception code 3221225477 (0xC0000005, access violation) for one parametrization of test_gather

key_errors: FAILED install\tests\layer_tests\tensorflow_tests\test_tf_Gather.py::TestGather::test_gather[ ie_device:CPU - precision:FP16 - indices_type:<class 'numpy.int32'> - params_type:<class 'numpy.float32'> - params:{'params_shape': [3, 2, 6, 4], 'indices_shape': [3, 2, 1, 3], 'axis_value': -1, 'batch_dims': -2, 'operation_type': 'GatherV2'} ] - multiprocessing.context.ProcessError: OpenVINO was killed with a signal 3221225477
E           multiprocessing.context.TimeoutError: OpenVINO running timed out!
= 1 failed, 5781 passed, 170 skipped, 15 xfailed, 2 xpassed, 25 warnings in 783.74s (0:13:03) =
root_cause: The TensorFlow layer test runs CPU inference for a Gather/GatherV2 case with a negative batch_dims (-2) and negative axis (-1), shapes params=[3,2,6,4], indices=[3,2,1,3]. The child worker process that executes OpenVINO inference (spawned via Python multiprocessing to isolate crashes) terminated abnormally with Windows exit code 3221225477 (0xC0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION), which the test harness first observed as a 60s queue-read timeout before reporting the ProcessError. This points to a native crash (likely an out-of-bounds memory access) inside the CPU Gather kernel or its shape/axis normalization logic when batch_dims is negative and resolves to the same effective axis as axis_value, rather than a test-harness or infra issue. No PR could be associated with this push (merge-queue commit from PR #39644, which touches NPUW blob handling and is unrelated to Gather); the failure is attributed to the CPU Gather implementation itself and may be a pre-existing latent bug newly exercised, or a flaky/race condition in that kernel path.
reproduction_steps: On a Windows build matching this CI config: cd install/tests/layer_tests && python -m pytest tensorflow_tests/test_tf_Gather.py::TestGather::test_gather -k "CPU and FP16 and batch_dims: -2" -v. If it does not reproduce immediately, loop the run (e.g. for /l %i in (1,1,20) do ...) since a 60s-timeout-then-crash pattern is consistent with either a rare crash or a slow/hung worker process; also try under a debugger or with AddressSanitizer-enabled CPU plugin build to capture the exact faulting instruction.
recommended_actions: Reproduce locally/in CI with the exact parametrization (CPU, FP16, GatherV2, params_shape=[3,2,6,4], indices_shape=[3,2,1,3], axis_value=-1, batch_dims=-2) and attach a debugger or enable Windows crash dumps to get a native stack trace for exit code 0xC0000005.

Inspect the CPU Gather node implementation (src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/gather.cpp) for how negative batch_dims/axis are normalized against the actual indices/data ranks, especially when axis and batch_dims end up referencing overlapping or out-of-range dimensions.

Check if this parametrization previously had an xfail/skip marker that was removed, and whether it reproduces consistently or only intermittently (run it 10-20x back-to-back to rule out a race condition).

If a genuine OOB write/read is found, add bounds validation or an explicit unsupported-combination check (batch_dims with axis resolving to the same effective dimension) rather than letting the kernel dereference invalid memory.
prevention_strategies: Add CPU-plugin-level ASan/UBSan nightly runs (or ensure existing ones cover Windows Gather kernels) so native memory-safety crashes like this surface with a stack trace instead of only a bare process exit code in layer tests. Extend Gather unit tests to explicitly cover negative batch_dims combined with negative axis values that resolve to the same effective dimension index, which appears to be an under-tested corner case.
historical_context: No prior pattern in the post-commit knowledge base matches this signature (searched for 'killed with a signal', '3221225477', '0xC0000005', 'access violation', and 'Gather' across all 50 existing pattern files — no hits). This is recorded as a new pattern for future recurrence tracking.
